verdicts.claim: DEVIATION 1 — Scope: the target is not a Cheon 2025 reproduction; it is a generic post-hoc SHAP wrapper with no cohort, label, CV, LightGBM training, forward selection or tuning (evidence: __init__.py:1-16; analyzer.py:1-13, 59-72, 112-129; grep for read_csv/KFold/fit(/roc_auc/forward/num_leaves returns no hits).
verdicts.reason: I re-ran the grep myself over both directories (all file types, __pycache__ excluded) with the pattern set read_csv|KFold|train_test_split|\.fit\(|roc_auc|forward|num_leaves|min_data_in_leaf|MMSE|CIST|activity_|sleep_|n_estimators|learning_rate|StratifiedKFold|GroupKFold. The ONLY four hits in either directory are the two illustrative table rows in each copy of USAGE.md. Every source file is explanation-side only: the constructor takes an already-fitted model and a name list, and explain() takes whatever X the caller hands it. diff -rq --exclude=__pycache__ between the two dirs exits 0 with no output, so the single audit applies to both. PAPER_PROTOCOL.md really does require the full pipeline the target lacks (l.23 '174 persons', l.52 'Total 12,183 daily records', l.78 '72 independent variables', l.150 'K-fold cross-validation, K = 5', l.141 Table 2 values).
verdicts.evidence: grep output over Taehyun/xai + Taehyun/previous/xai: only 'xai/USAGE.md:172:| CN | raw_sleep_score_rem | 0.0421 | -0.0103 |' and 'xai/USAGE.md:179:| raw_sleep_score_rem | 0.0398 |' (and the same two lines in previous/xai). analyzer.py:112-114 'def explain(self, X) -> "ShapAnalyzer": ... X_arr, X_pandas = _coerce_input(X, self.feature_names)'. analyzer.py:119 'self._adapter = TreeAdapter(self.model)' — the model arrives pre-fitted.

verdicts.claim: DEVIATION 2 — Class framing: the package defaults to multiclass with n_classes=3 and class_names CN/MCI/Dementia, whereas the paper is binary CN vs MCI+Dem (evidence: analyzer.py:65-66; USAGE.md:41-42, 78-79, 118-119).
verdicts.reason: Both cited lines are exactly as claimed, and all three USAGE.md sites show the 3-class CN/MCI/Dementia example. One qualification the reader should have added: these are constructor DEFAULTS, not a hard-coded framing — 'binary' is an accepted task value (analyzer.py:78) and the only caller of this package inside the repo (Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:155, outside the audited dirs) overrides them to task="binary", n_classes=1. So the deviation is a default/documentation deviation, not an inability to do the paper's binary task.
verdicts.evidence: analyzer.py:65-66 'task: str = "multiclass",' / 'n_classes: int = 3,'. USAGE.md:41-42 'n_classes=3,' / 'class_names=["CN", "MCI", "Dementia"],' (repeated verbatim at 78-79 and 118-119). Counter-context: Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:155 'ShapAnalyzer(model=base_model, feature_names=all_feats, task="binary", n_classes=1, class_names=["Dementia"])'.

verdicts.claim: DEVIATION 3 — SHAP is computed on whatever X the caller passes, documented as X_test; the paper does not report which data SHAP used (evidence: analyzer.py:112-122; USAGE.md:45, 82, 125).
verdicts.reason: All three USAGE.md line numbers are exact, and explain() has no notion of train/test — it stores whatever array it is given. The reference's 'NOT REPORTED' status is also exactly as the reader states.
verdicts.evidence: USAGE.md:45 'analyzer.explain(X_test)'; USAGE.md:82 'analyzer.explain(X_test)                  # DataFrame 그대로 OK'; USAGE.md:125 'analyzer.explain(X_test_scaled)          # (N, 7, 71)'. analyzer.py:115-116 'self._X_explained = X_arr' / 'self._X_pandas = X_pandas'. PAPER_PROTOCOL.md:124 'SHAP explainer type, data used for SHAP, aggregation ... | NOT REPORTED'.

verdicts.claim: DEVIATION 4 — The package hints at a caller-side 71-feature, raw_-prefixed feature set with 7-day sequences, versus the paper's 72 Figure-2 features on day-level rows (evidence: USAGE.md:109, 115, 172, 179, 248).
verdicts.reason: The strings are all present, so the claim is literally true, with two caveats the reader should have flagged. (a) One citation is off by one: line 115 is 'model=keras_model,'; the '길이 71' comment is on line 116. (b) The '71 features / raw_ prefix' hint belongs to the Keras-LSTM example only, and 'raw_ prefix naming scheme' is generalized from a single illustrative table row whose numbers the reader elsewhere (correctly) calls placeholders. The package defines no features at all, and the actual caller derives its feature list from dataframe columns at run time, so neither 71 nor any naming scheme is a choice made inside the audit target.
verdicts.evidence: USAGE.md:109 '`train_lstm_colab.py` 산출물 기준. 입력은 3D `(N, 7, 71)`.'; USAGE.md:116 'feature_names=feature_names,         # 길이 71' (NOT 115, which is 'model=keras_model,'); USAGE.md:172/179 'raw_sleep_score_rem'; USAGE.md:248 '`(N, 7, 71)` 배열 반환'. Contrast, outside the audited dirs: Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:140 'all_features = [col for col in train_df.columns if col not in DROP_COLS]'.

verdicts.claim: ERROR 1 — task='binary' or 'regression' with the default n_classes=3 raises IndexError in per_class_values(): _slice_classes returns a 1-element list but the dict comprehension enumerates 3 default class_names (evidence: analyzer.py:65-66, 93-97, 147-148, 306-307).
verdicts.reason: Every cited line is exact and the failure follows from the code alone, with no library-version dependency. With task='binary' and class_names omitted, self.class_names = ['class_0','class_1','class_2'] (3 entries, since n_classes defaults to 3), while _slice_classes returns [raw] (1 entry); the comprehension indexes sliced[1] -> IndexError. The length guard that would have caught this is disabled for non-multiclass tasks by its own 'and task == "multiclass"' clause (analyzer.py:98-99), a line the reader did not cite. The break propagates to aggregated_values(), to_dataframe(), save_plots() and analyze(), i.e. every output path. Note it is also triggered by the natural binary call ShapAnalyzer(..., task='binary', class_names=['CN','Impaired']) with n_classes left at 3.
verdicts.evidence: analyzer.py:306-307 'if task != "multiclass":' / '    return [raw]'. analyzer.py:147-148 'sliced = _slice_classes(self._raw_shap, self.n_classes, self.task)' / 'return {name: sliced[i] for i, name in enumerate(self.class_names)}'. analyzer.py:98 'if len(self.class_names) != n_classes and task == "multiclass":' — the guard never fires for binary.

verdicts.claim: ERROR 2 — For binary sklearn RF/ExtraTrees under shap>=0.45 the TreeExplainer output is (N, F, 2); with task='binary' the class axis is never sliced, so aggregate_time_axis collapses axis=1 (the FEATURE axis) and importance_dataframe then fails on a feature-count mismatch (or silently produces a 2-column result if plots are skipped).
verdicts.reason: The internal branch is exactly as described and I confirm it: for task != 'multiclass' the raw array is passed through unsliced, and aggregate_time_axis blindly treats any 3-D array as (N, T, F) and means over axis=1. But the claimed OUTCOME is not determinable from the code. It depends entirely on which layout the installed shap returns, and the package pins no shap version and ships no requirements file — the code itself documents both layouts as possible (explainers.py:76-79). Under the other documented layout, the list branch, _to_ndarray stacks to (C, N, F); axis=1 is then the SAMPLE axis, so the result is (2, F), which PASSES the feature-count check at outputs.py:43 and yields a silently wrong DataFrame that raises nothing — the opposite of the claimed mismatch error. The reader's parenthetical 'silently produces a 2-column result' is also wrong as written: a (N,2) array is rejected, not silently accepted, by outputs.py:43-47. Finally, reachability is not as stated: with the reader's own error #1, task='binary' with the default n_classes=3 dies earlier at IndexError, so this path needs n_classes=1 — which is, notably, exactly what the one in-repo caller passes.
verdicts.evidence: analyzer.py:306-307 'if task != "multiclass": return [raw]' (no class slicing) and aggregation.py:46-47 'if mode == "abs_mean": return np.mean(np.abs(shap_values), axis=1)' — branch confirmed. Undecidable premise: explainers.py:77-79 '- list[ndarray] 길이 C : 멀티클래스 (구버전 shap)  → stack → (C, ...)' / '- ndarray (..., C)     : 멀티클래스 (shap >= 0.45)'; explainers.py:81-82 'if isinstance(raw, list): return np.stack([np.asarray(r) for r in raw], axis=0)'. No version pin exists (USAGE.md:19 '- `shap` (pip install shap)'; no requirements/setup file in either directory).

verdicts.claim: ERROR 3 — save_plots(per_class=False) averages SIGNED SHAP across classes (near-degenerate for probability-output models), while to_dataframe(combine_classes=False) averages mean_abs_shap, so the two 'class-average' outputs are inconsistent (evidence: analyzer.py:214-223 vs 178-186).
verdicts.reason: The inconsistency is real and both citations are exact. For the paper-relevant tree path the per-class arrays are 2-D and aggregate_time_axis returns them unchanged (aggregation.py:36-37), so the values np.stack/np.mean averages at analyzer.py:216 are signed, whereas the DataFrame branch averages the already-absolute mean_abs_shap column. One qualification: 'signed' holds for 2-D (tree) input; for 3-D sequence input with the default aggregation='abs_mean' the values are already non-negative before the class average, so the two paths disagree only in the tree case. The 'near-degenerate' consequence is a property of probability-output SHAP (sums to ~0 across classes), not something the code states — and it would NOT apply to LightGBM multiclass, whose TreeExplainer default is raw margin. The reader hedged this correctly with 'e.g. sklearn RF' and low confidence.
verdicts.evidence: analyzer.py:215-216 '# 클래스 평균 = 클래스 축으로 stack 후 평균' / 'stacked = np.mean(np.stack(list(per_class_vals.values()), axis=0), axis=0)'. analyzer.py:181-182 '.groupby("feature", as_index=False)' / '.agg(mean_abs_shap=("mean_abs_shap", "mean"))'. aggregation.py:36-37 'if shap_values.ndim == 2:' / '    return shap_values' — tree values reach line 216 signed.

verdicts.claim: ERROR 4 — Leakage risk is delegated to the caller: the documented recipe computes the importance ranking on X_test; if a caller then selects features from that ranking and reports on the same X_test, selection is fit on evaluation rows. The package performs no split, so this is a usage hazard, not a bug in the target.
verdicts.reason: The two factual halves are verified: USAGE.md's worked recipes do pass X_test, and there is no split, seed-for-split, or hold-out anywhere in the package (my grep for KFold|StratifiedKFold|GroupKFold|train_test_split over both dirs returns nothing; the only random_state seeds the Keras background subsample). The hypothetical, however, is not realized by the one caller that exists in this repo: Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py explains on X_train and then runs its forward selection under StratifiedKFold on that same training frame — which happens to match the reference's A14 ('explained on the same rows used for fitting'), not the X_test recipe the reader worried about. The reader flagged the risk from the docs alone without checking the caller; the claim survives as stated only because it is explicitly framed as a hazard rather than a defect.
verdicts.evidence: USAGE.md:45/82/125 'analyzer.explain(X_test)' / 'analyzer.explain(X_test_scaled)'. analyzer.py:259 'rng = np.random.default_rng(self.random_state)' is the sole use of the seed. Not realized in practice: Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:156-157 'analyzer.explain(X_train)' / 'shap_df = analyzer.to_dataframe(combine_classes=False)'; ASSUMPTIONS.md:22 (A14) '... explained on the same rows used for fitting'.

missed_items: The two callers USAGE.md names DO NOT EXIST anywhere in the repository. The reader wrote that LightGBM_RF_Model.py (USAGE.md:69) and train_lstm_colab.py (USAGE.md:109) are 'outside the audited directories', implying they exist; a repo-wide `find -iname '*LightGBM_RF_Model*' -o -iname '*train_lstm*'` returns nothing. The only file in the repository that imports the package is /Users/pig30nidae/Pig30nidaE/AJOU/26-1-summer/Google-AJOU-AI-Capstone/Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:39 'from xai import ShapAnalyzer'. The reader audited the package without ever locating its real caller.

That caller is the Cheon-shaped pipeline, and it changes the reading of both of the reader's top errors. Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:155 'ShapAnalyzer(model=base_model, feature_names=all_feats, task="binary", n_classes=1, class_names=["Dementia"])' — n_classes=1 with a 1-element class_names is precisely the configuration that DODGES the reader's error #1 (IndexError) and simultaneously ACTIVATES the unsliced-3-D path of error #2. The reader graded #1 'high' and #2 'medium' on the defaults alone, with the priority ordering reversed relative to actual use. (Cited for context; this file is outside the audited directories.)

Protocol facts visible in that caller, all unreported by the reader: SHAP is computed on TRAINING rows (Binary_LGBM_RF.py:156 'analyzer.explain(X_train)'), the ranking feeds a forward-selection loop under 'StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)' (l.166, again l.228), the ranking model is 'LGBMClassifier(random_state=42, n_jobs=-1, class_weight="balanced")' (l.152), and the split is the AI-Hub Training/Validation partitions used as train/test ('train_df = train_merged...' / 'test_df = val_merged...', l.135-136) rather than the pooled 12,183-record cohort of ASSUMPTIONS.md A02. Feature count is data-derived, not fixed (l.140-142).

No shap version pin and no dependency file, which is the package's single largest correctness exposure. Neither directory contains requirements.txt / setup.py / pyproject.toml (only 6 .py files plus USAGE.md), and USAGE.md:19 says only '- `shap` (pip install shap)'. Yet the class-axis handling is explicitly version-branching — explainers.py:77-79 documents both the pre-0.45 list layout and the >=0.45 trailing-axis layout, and _slice_classes guesses between leading and trailing axes at analyzer.py:310-315. The reader noted the shap>=0.45 shape in passing inside one error but never reported the missing pin as a finding.

A documented aggregation mode is broken on the main output path. aggregation='none' is exported in AGGREGATIONS (aggregation.py:21), documented in the mode table (USAGE.md:152) and recommended in the FAQ (USAGE.md:247-248), but it makes aggregated_values() return a 3-D array, which importance_dataframe rejects: outputs.py:41-42 'if shap_2d.ndim != 2: raise ValueError(f"Expected 2D shap values, got shape {shap_2d.shape}")'. save_plots() would likewise hand a 3-D array to shap.summary_plot. Not reported by the reader.

The root cause of the reader's own error #1 was not cited: analyzer.py:98 'if len(self.class_names) != n_classes and task == "multiclass":' — the class_names/n_classes consistency check is switched off for exactly the tasks (binary, regression) where the mismatch is fatal. The reader cited the defaults and the crash site but not the disabled guard.

Sequence-model plots mix two different aggregations, unreported. SHAP is collapsed with abs_mean by default (analyzer.py:70, aggregation.py:47) while the feature matrix underlying the same plot is a plain time-mean of X: analyzer.py:273-274 'if X.ndim == 3:' / '    return np.mean(X, axis=1)'. With abs_mean every plotted SHAP value is non-negative, so the 'summary'/'beeswarm' outputs (outputs.py:99-112) are one-sided by construction rather than the signed distributions those plot types denote.

Nothing implements the paper's dementia risk score or its statistics, and the reader's 'statistics: not applicable' did not name this gap. PAPER_PROTOCOL.md:204-206 defines Score = sum of positive SHAP values per daily record, with CN mean 7.59 vs impaired mean 15.71 and a one-sample one-sided t-test. The package only ever reduces over the sample axis (outputs.py:50-52 'mean_abs = np.mean(np.abs(shap_2d), axis=0)' / 'mean_signed = np.mean(shap_2d, axis=0)') and exposes no per-record positive-SHAP sum, so the paper's Eq. 2 pathway is absent as well as the pipeline.

SHAP output space is left to the library default and a fresh explainer is rebuilt on every call: explainers.py:39 'self.explainer = shap_lib.TreeExplainer(model)' with no model_output/feature_perturbation argument, invoked from analyzer.py:119 inside explain(). This is what makes the reader's own error #3 degeneracy model-dependent (raw margin for LightGBM vs probability for sklearn RF); the reader asserted the consequence without noting that the output space is unspecified in the code.

Minor doc/code contradiction not reported: outputs.py:78 states the backend is forced ('matplotlib backend는 Agg로 강제'), but outputs.py:83 is 'matplotlib.use("Agg", force=False)', which leaves an already-selected interactive backend in place — the headless guarantee the docstring promises is not actually provided.

Housekeeping the reader stated without showing: I independently verified 'diff -rq --exclude=__pycache__' between the two directories exits 0 with no output, and that previous/xai/__pycache__ holds only cpython-312/313/314 bytecode for the same six modules (no orphaned .pyc revealing a deleted source file). The reader's byte-identical claim holds.
